The obstruction to dimensional reduction is gauge--geometry entanglement: transverse magnetic fields on a two-dimensional (2D) surface and structural torsion on a one-dimensional (1D) curve couple the tangential dynamics to the transverse degrees of freedom. We remove this entanglement by three mechanisms---a generalized transverse Poincar\'{e} gauge, the rotation-minimizing Bishop frame, and the parity of the transverse ground state, the last of which annihilates the residual first-order magnetic coupling for a single inversion-symmetric well. On a torus, an axial field generates a joint Sagnac--Aharonov--Bohm residual of tunable sign without spoiling the poloidal--azimuthal separability, whereas an in-plane field couples only through the out-of-plane extent of the structure: it breaks the axial symmetry there but leaves a planar curve unaffected to first order. The same torus shows the axial field tuning the curvature-induced localization, and a corrugated quantum ring converts periodic geometric and flux modulations into an artificial superlattice whose in-plane-field immunity follows from planarity and parity, not from the smallness of the field. Non-inertial quantum dynamics on surfaces and curves of arbitrary shape is thus reduced, within the thin-layer regime, to two ingredients: an effective gauge potential and a geometric potential.

papers.title: Exponential Analysis for Trace-Distance Errors in Quantum Information Theory
papers.abstract: We study the trace-distance error in classical-quantum soft covering, privacy amplification against quantum side information, convex splitting, and decoupling by a Haar-random unitary followed by partial trace. In the independent and identically distributed setting, we determine exact reliability functions and strong converse exponents for soft covering with independent codewords, uniform convex splitting, and Haar partial-trace decoupling. For privacy amplification, we determine the exact reliability function for independent random binning and the exact strong converse exponent for every two-universal hash ensemble. The reliability and strong converse formulas involve sandwiched and Petz-R\'enyi information, respectively. The proofs connect trace-distance errors to quantum hypothesis testing, using Rosenthal inequalities for sums of random matrices in the reliability analysis and conditional second-moment bounds for the strong converses.

papers.title: Noise threshold for learning with quantum memory
papers.abstract: A quantum memory can reduce exponentially the number of experiments needed to learn a physical process, but real memories are noisy. Here we show that, for Pauli memory noise with eigenvalues $\lambda_X,\lambda_Y,\lambda_Z$, the advantage is governed by $\lambda_X^2+\lambda_Y^2+\lambda_Z^2$. We prove that no protocol with an entangled probe gains an exponential advantage when this sum is at most one, reduce the general case to the additivity of a R\'enyi-2 coherent information, and find coded memories that retain a growing advantage within 1% of this threshold. On a superconducting processor, nine simultaneously operated Bell pairs show an advantage that grows or shrinks exponentially with system size, reversing where a parameter-free model predicts. A three-qubit repetition code turns a shrinking advantage into a growing one with all processor and readout errors included, and under dephasing its memory performs better than Bell sampling in any memory frame on a perfect processor.

papers.title: High-Throughput GPU Decoding of Quantum Bivariate Bicycle Codes under Circuit-Level Noise
papers.abstract: Bivariate bicycle (BB) codes reduce the physical-qubit overhead of quantum error correction compared to other codes such as Surface codes, but circuit-level faults create dependencies across measurement rounds that limit decoding throughput. We present a parallel-window GPU decoder that combines reusable fault patterns, compact shared-memory state, and persistent GPU workers using min-sum with Relay-BP recovery. On an RTX 5090, the proposed decoder keeps pace with one syndrome round every 1 $\mu$s across all four evaluated codes, up to [[144,12,12]] with 63-144 $\mu$s median commit delays. This rate has not been demonstrated in prior circuit-level GPU decoding studies and it provides $120\times$ higher decoding throughput than sequential sliding-window decoding. Checking neighboring detector rounds before accepting a decoding result reduces failure rates by up to 65%. For [[144,12,12]] at $p=0.002$, our proposed decoder achieves $7.58\times 10^{-6}$ failures per round, 36% lower than the published belief propagation (BP) with syndrome flipping (BP-SF) result.

papers.title: Resource theory of pi-ordered imaginarity and its resource quantifiers
papers.abstract: Conventional resource theory of quantum imaginarity takes real density matrices as free states without ordering constraints on their diagonal populations. Motivated by the role of population ordering in the incoherent ergotropy of quantum batteries and the recently proposed framework of $\pi$-ordered coherence, we develop the resource theory of $\pi$-ordered imaginarity. In this refined framework, free states are required to be real in the reference basis and to obey a prescribed permutation order $\pi$ for their diagonal populations. This theory thereby identifies two independent quantum resources: complex phases and population misordering, where the latter is inaccessible within the standard imaginarity resource theory. We characterize the structure of free states using majorization and the Schur-Horn theorem, define admissible $\pi$-ordered real operations, and examine their intersection with $\pi$-ordered incoherent operations. We further construct resource quantifiers for the $\pi$-ordered imaginarity based on relative entropy, fidelity and robustness, and derive inequalities relating the robustness of $\pi$-ordered imaginarity and that of $\pi$-ordered coherence. The present framework generalizes the standard resource theory of imaginarity to incorporate population ordering and is naturally suited for thermodynamic settings such as quantum batteries.

papers.title: Dynamics of a Charged Particle on a Conformal Helicoidal Surface
papers.abstract: We study the classical and quantum motion of a charged particle on a conformal helicoidal surface embedded in four-dimensional Euclidean space. A uniform ambient magnetic field pulls back to a nonuniform surface field. The cyclic longitudinal coordinate permits an exact transverse reduction. The ordinary helicoid in the same axial field shares the effective potential and the turning points, while the conformal metric increases the physical period at matched energy and longitudinal momentum. We classify the single- and double-well regimes and obtain the exact transverse periods in the two double-well sectors. The periods diverge logarithmically at the separatrix, with twice the leading coefficient above the barrier as below it. The zero-field limit allows transverse escape, and the weak-twist limit is locally free but nonuniform across the surface. Intrinsic quantization gives an exact weighted transverse eigenvalue problem. Fixed-momentum eigenvalues test the harmonic approximation in a central well and resolve the tunneling splittings in a double well.

papers.title: Why do single photons produce interference fringes? The phase of a mode and the phase of a state
papers.abstract: If the phase of a photon-number state is completely undetermined, how can single photons, sent one at a time through a two-slit apparatus, build up interference fringes? These lecture notes answer this question from first principles. Starting from Maxwell's equations, we expand the field in vector modes, quantize it, and introduce the quantity measured by a photodetector. We then show that the word ``phase'' refers to two different things: the phase of a mode, fixed by the optical setup, and the phase of the quantum state that excites the mode. Only the first determines the fringes. All calculations are given in full, and problems with solutions are included.

papers.title: LatentRL-QAS: Transfer via Latent Reinforcement Learning for Quantum Architecture Search
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) emerges as a prominent approach to quantum architecture search (QAS), the automated design of quantum circuits. However, transferring what an agent has learned from one number of qubits to another is still weakly explored: the state, the action space and the neural network of a state-of-the-art RL-QAS agent all grow with the number of qubits, which makes transfer learning across qubit counts prohibitive. We make this transfer possible by introducing LatentRL-QAS, a latent space transfer and refresh framework for RL-based QAS. At its core, a circuit variational autoencoder encodes a circuit as one token per gate and maps circuits on any number of qubits into the same latent space. An RL agent navigates this space instead of adding gates, so its state, actions and network have the same size at every qubit count. The latent space is periodically refreshed with the agent's new discoveries and, for a larger system, grown from the solutions of the smaller one, so what is transferred is the representation of circuits, not network weights or past experience. To show transfer, we consider absolutely maximally entangled (AME) states, a resource for quantum error correction. LatentRL-QAS discovers the five- and six-qubit AME states without being shown them and prepares them in 89-99% of evaluation episodes, whereas the baseline RL-QAS fails to find them with the same budget, even with a network 10 to 17 times larger. LatentRL-QAS remains robust under depolarizing noise with single-qubit gate errors amplified 10x and two-qubit gate errors 5x compared with IBM quantum hardware. By decoupling the RL agent from the number of qubits, LatentRL-QAS lets quantum architecture search reuse circuit representations learned on smaller problems, providing a foundation for the transferable design of circuits across quantum optimization problems.

papers.title: Magic Moments: An Operational Approach of Certifying Nonstabilizerness from Few Copies
papers.abstract: Magic is the key resource enabling universal fault-tolerant quantum computation beyond classically simulable stabilizer circuits. Certifying it, however, usually requires either full state tomography or an optimization over the set of stabilizer states, both of which rapidly become prohibitive as the system grows. Here, we introduce a moment-based criterion that certifies magic from a few moments of the discrete Wigner function, without fully reconstructing the distribution itself. For pure states of any number of qudits the criterion is necessary and sufficient, while for mixed states we construct a hierarchy of higher moments conditions that reaches the exact negativity threshold. We also derive lower bounds on sum negativity and mana from low-order moments, and use them to bound the negativity factor in quasiprobability simulation. Each moment can be evaluated as the expectation value of a two-outcome observable on a few copies of the state, measurable with a constant-depth Clifford circuit and a number of rounds independent of qudit number, providing efficient, experimentally accessible tools for certifying and quantifying nonstabilizer resources.

papers.title: Slow mixing of Gibbs sampling for the quantum Curie-Weiss model
papers.abstract: Hamiltonian evolution can spread local operators across a dense quantum magnet. We show that this global support does not remove the bottleneck to thermalization in the quantum Curie-Weiss model: at fixed low temperature and weak transverse field, the Chen-Kastoryano-Gilyen Gibbs sampler [arXiv: 2311.09207] has an exponentially large mixing-time lower bound. A dynamical quantum bottleneck theory that generalizes the classical notion of conductance has been proposed alongside existing frameworks that rely on spatial locality. We also give a complementary interpretation of slow mixing using an effective Fokker-Planck equation.

papers.title: Experimental Quantum Hardware Benchmarks of Flat Non-Clifford Hypergraph States, Antipodal Obstructions, and Nonlocal Games on IBM Heron r2
papers.abstract: Real-hardware demonstrations of quantum contextuality have reached high precision on superconducting processors, exemplified by Google Quantum AI's Mermin-Peres magic square and stabilizer games on Willow (Science, 2026). Extending such benchmarks beyond the Clifford regime requires non-Clifford hypergraph states |\psi_f> = 2^{-n/2} \sum_x (-1)^{f(x)} |x> governed by discrete algebraic invariants. Building on our Lean 4-verified framework of Modular Walsh Rigidity and Antipodal Obstructions, we present an experimental study on two 156-qubit IBM Heron r2 processors (ibm_fez, ibm_kingston) across 3 to 50 qubits and 11 auditable jobs (2.13 RUs total). First, we verify antipodal obstructions and mod-17 Walsh rigidity for degree-3/4 states (n=6,8,10), observing 5.4x-11.6x X-basis flatness separation between bent states, obstructed controls, and a degree-4 mod-3 fooler (W = +-1 mod 3), plus n=7 nonlinearity extraction (54.83 vs. 56.00). Second, barrier-protected Loschmidt echoes confirm non-Clifford coherence up to genuinely entangled 16-qubit degree-4 states (1,488x above random on ibm_fez; 17,296x on ibm_kingston for 2x8q, a 2.87x cross-chip gain) and locate a Heavy-Hex depth-513 coherence cliff. Third, calibration-aware layout raises the raw Mermin-Peres win rate on ibm_fez to 96.85 +- 0.09% raw (+87.4 sigma above 88.89% classical; 1.45 pp below Willow's 98.30% raw), while a tensored SPAM diagnostic reaches 98.35%. Uniformly random even-weight GHZ parity games beat the classical bound up to n=30 (89.44% [+79.4 sigma] at 6q to 59.46 +- 0.54% [+17.4 sigma] at 30q). Finally, 3-qubit CCZ rotated Mermin-3 (83.95 +- 0.29%, +31.2 sigma) and Hardy/Guhne-Cabello (77.15 +- 0.33%, +6.5 sigma) games strictly violate the exhaustive 75.00% LHV ceiling, and degree-3/4 antipodal parity witnesses achieve up to +45.87 pp (n=12) and +35.79 pp joint advantage on connected 16-qubit degree-4 states.

papers.title: Direct generation of N00N states with layered semiconductors
papers.abstract: Photonic N00N states enable phase sensing beyond the classical limit, but their generation conventionally relies on interferometric manipulation of photons using bulk optical components. Here we demonstrate the direct generation of a family of tunable two-photon polarization N00N states from a subwavelength-thick 3R-MoS2 flake. For propagation along the optic axis, the in-plane crystal symmetry allows all symmetry permitted spontaneous parametric down-conversion pathway to interfere coherently, while the large second-order nonlinearity provides sufficient brightness at submicrometer thickness without phase matching. The pump polarization sets the basis of the N00N state or equivalently a two-photon Holland-Burnett state without altering its structure or the generation efficiency. The biphotons are highly indistinguishable, reach high fidelity with the target state across a wide range of pump polarizations, and show two-photon interference fringes with visibilities above the threshold for the postselected phase supersensitivity. Our theoretical analysis further indicates that, in the ideal single-mode limit, the same interaction would yield higher-order Holland-Burnett states. By eliminating interferometric stages, our results establish a compact, pump-programmable source for quantum-enhanced polarization interferometry

papers.title: Unitary Synthesis with a Unary Tracker
papers.abstract: This manuscript studies general unitary synthesis using unary-encoded ancillary register. Our first construction focuses on the $T$-cost of unitary synthesis. We maintain a unary register that coherently tracks the computational-basis label of the data. This allows Boolean lookups to use only CNOTs and shares the precision-dependent synthesis cost across the branches of each cosine-sine decomposition (CSD) factor. For a classically specified $n$-qubit unitary with $K$ mixing branches in its CSD, we obtain $T$-count $O(K+NL)$ using $N+O(L)$ clean ancillas, where $N=2^n$ and $L=n+\log(1/\epsilon)$. We also give a related construction that directly applies the unitary onto a unary register to implement disjoint branches in parallel. Combining this with the quantum Shannon decomposition gives space-depth volume $O(N^2)$ using arbitrary single-qubit gates and CNOTs, which matches the asymptotically optimal bound.

papers.title: Sharp Transitions of Copy Complexity in Local Certification of Typical Pure States
papers.abstract: We determine the asymptotic copy complexity of $n$-qudit state certification with tensor-product measurements. For given acceptance and rejection fidelities $a$ and $b$ ($b<a$), the optimal copy complexity is $\Theta(n^r)$. For each qudit dimension $d$, $r$ is a piecewise constant function of $g=(a-b)/(1-b)$. This scaling holds for a family of sets of pure target states whose Haar measures tend to one as $n\to\infty$. We characterize the range of $g$ corresponding to each optimal exponent and provide an algorithm for computing its endpoints exactly. The optimal exponent grows logarithmically with $1/g$ as $g$ tends to zero. The upper bound is achieved by a nonadaptive protocol using only single-qudit projective measurements and classical postprocessing. The matching lower bound is established by constructing pairs of states that are difficult to distinguish under arbitrary tensor-product measurements. Our result can thus guide the design of certification tests when the number of available copies is limited.

papers.title: Fewer Parameters, Longer Runtimes: The Wall-Clock Cost of Hybrid Quantum Physics-Informed Neural Networks
papers.abstract: While hybrid quantum-classical physics-informed neural networks (QCPINNs) are often described as efficient because they have fewer trainable parameters than classical PINNs, parameter count does not measure wall-clock cost. To examine this gap on a one-dimensional seawater temperature diffusion benchmark, with the quantum circuits simulated on a CPU, we time the four cumulative stages a PINN needs (the forward pass, the first- and second-order input gradients, and the PDE-loss parameter gradient) for a classical PINN, four hybrid configurations that differ in qubit count and circuit depth, and size-matched classical controls that share the hybrids' classical layers. We find that the hybrids are 14-56x slower than the classical PINN for the forward pass and 10-97x slower for the PDE-loss parameter gradient, and even against the size-matched controls, they remain 9-85x slower. Further, over the tested ranges, runtime increased approximately exponentially with qubit count, approximately linearly with circuit depth, and sub-linearly with batch size, while for the circuit-only forward pass, a second simulator backend was 10-165x slower under the same calling pattern. Although the hybrids have 38-44% fewer parameters than the classical PINN, this reduction comes from their smaller classical layers, as the quantum circuit accounts for at most 2.5% of each hybrid's parameters. Yet parameter count failed to predict runtime even among the classical networks, since the size-matched controls, despite having fewer parameters than the classical PINN, run slower than it. Our conclusion is that fewer parameters did not mean lower cost: every hybrid took at least ten times longer than the classical PINN at every stage, and the gap grew quickly with the number of qubits.

papers.title: The integrable Lie-Trotter-Suzuki decomposition for nonlinear dynamics: Efficient Hamiltonian simulation of the Stepanoff flow
papers.abstract: We propose an efficient unitary numerical time integration strategy for nonlinear dynamical systems: the integrable Lie-Trotter-Suzuki decomposition (I-LTS). First, express the generator as a sum of integrable parts. Second, approximate the full evolution operator using a Lie-Trotter-Suzuki (LTS) decomposition of the desired approximation order in time step. The I-LTS construction ensures that the full evolution operator can be represented as a product of terms that each have an efficient explicit tensor product factorization that can be handled efficiently with tensor network and/or quantum block-encoding methods. Next, we apply this method to an important non-integrable point example of a dynamical system: the Stepanoff flow on the torus. First, we derive an efficient unitary quantum algorithm for simulating the Stepanoff flow that can be thought of as a unitary classical version of a quantum map. Then, we provide a detailed description of the encoding of the two-dimensional system into an efficient quantum circuit, including an efficient block-encoding for all required operators. An efficient Hamiltonian simulation algorithm is constructed using a sequence of alternating quantum Fourier transforms (QFT) and Quantum Signal Processing (QSP) circuits. Finally, the circuit is simulated using a numerical emulator of fault-tolerant quantum computers, and the results are found to be consistent with several alternative classical computational methods. While efficient, the need for Trotterization introduces fundamental complexity in requiring small enough time step for an accurate approximation and solving for the transfer operator requires one to confront the linear scaling of the advection operator with grid size.

papers.title: Rugosity as a measurement-induced relative entropy
papers.abstract: Quantum-state rugosity quantifies the departure of a quantum state from the flat superposition associated with a prescribed basis. We show that rugosity equals the classical relative entropy generated by the binary flat-state measurement. This identity gives two hypothesis-testing interpretations. Rugosity is the asymptotic discrimination exponent under repeated flat-state measurements and the exact finite-copy exponent under unrestricted quantum testing with zero type-I error. For smoothly parametrized states, we relate its local variation to the Fisher information accessible through the prescribed measurement. Using the local expansion of quantum relative entropy, we derive a bound on rugosity sensitivity in terms of the entropy-production susceptibility of a subsequent thermal reset. This susceptibility is given by the Bogoliubov-Kubo-Mori Fisher information. Finally, we formulate a measurement-dependent quantum speed limit whose endpoint distinguishability is determined by rugosity. These results connect quantum-state rugosity with statistical discrimination, thermal reset, and the geometry of experimentally accessible probability distributions.

papers.title: Monotone Crossing Lattices for Exact Binary Optimization Encodings on Rydberg Arrays
papers.abstract: Programmable Rydberg-atom arrays realize maximum-weight independent set encoding on unit-disk graphs under the ideal blockade model, but embedding nonlocal interactions requires auxiliary atoms and limits the size of tractable instances. We introduce a four-state unit-disk crossing cell that couples directly to adjacent cells, with interfaces enforcing one-sided propagation: along occupied paths directed away from the diagonal, copy bits are nondecreasing. For the maximum-weight independent set problem, uniform cell weights guarantee that every ground state of the encoded instance decodes to an optimal solution of the original problem, even when local copies disagree. For binary quadratic objectives subject to pairwise Boolean constraints, every feasible optimum yields consistent active copies and a target weight given by an explicit constant offset minus the source objective. A rectangular variant of the architecture further encodes minimum set cover problem. Prior to constraint-induced site deletions, the full layout requires $2n^2 - n$ sites, halving the leading-order site count of a fixed complete-grid reference, while activity pruning yields an exact site count set by the propagation span. Across 18 paired benchmarks with independent ordering from a shared candidate pool, the layout reduces site counts by 12.1%-54.0%.

papers.title: State convertibility in quantum-state texture from a general form of free operations
papers.abstract: State convertibility specifies which transformations between states a quantum resource theory allows. In quantum-state texture, deterministic conversion criteria are known for qubits and pure sources in arbitrary dimension, but a general criterion for mixed states in higher dimensions is missing. We derive this exact criterion from a complete characterization of free operations in arbitrary finite dimension. Because the unique free state is pure, every free operation splits into a quantum filter and a residual completely positive map. Using this decomposition, we show that every allowed conversion admits a two-outcome measurement that retains the filtered state after one outcome and prepares a fixed state after the other. Conversion thus reduces to finding such a filter whose unnormalized output leaves a positive semidefinite remainder when subtracted from the target, a search we show to be solvable by semidefinite programming. Beyond deterministic conversion, the characterization of free operations can be used to study probabilistic and assisted manipulation of quantum-state texture. More broadly, since the construction relies on a pure fixed state, it also applies to other resource theories defined by free operations fixing such a state.

papers.title: Simultaneous computation of multiple excited states via double bracket flows
papers.abstract: Efficient computation of excited states is essential for studying strongly correlated many-body systems and molecular electronic structure. In this work, we propose a framework for simultaneously simulating multiple excited states based on dynamical flows. The main idea is to exploit a common double bracket flow that drives different pure initial states toward different target excited states without such prior information. We establish a necessary condition for convergence and a sufficient condition for exponential convergence. We further develop two scheduling strategies: Chebyshev scheduling, which achieves optimal convergence near a fixed point but requires prior spectral information, and adaptive scheduling, which achieves comparable performance in numerical simulations without spectral information. Our results enable new classical and quantum algorithms for excited-state computation without prior preparation of lower-energy eigenstates.

papers.title: Bound magic in multi-qubit systems
papers.abstract: Magic captures nonstabilizerness, a resource required for quantum computational speedups. We prove the existence of multi-qubit nonstabilizer states from which no pure magic can be distilled, even with arbitrarily many copies and rounds of stabilizer operations. Such bound magic states have previously been only known to exist in odd Hilbert-space dimensions, where positivity of discrete Wigner functions can be used analogously to the positive partial transpose (PPT) criterion for bound entanglement. We introduce a PPT analogue for magic in multi-qubit systems that is closed under tensor products and stabilizer operations and reduces to the stabilizer polytope for one and two qubits. This enables the proof of multi-qubit bound magic and the explicit construction of bound magic states for $n \geq 3$ qubits.

papers.title: Exact monogamy of steering and remote Wigner negativity for multimode Gaussian nodes
papers.abstract: Optical quantum networks route correlations through nodes that hold several modes and are linked to many neighbors. Steering is the correlation behind one-sided device-independent tasks and behind the remote preparation of non-Gaussian states. It is monogamous for a single mode, which can be steered by only one party, but how many neighbors can steer a node with $k$ modes was not known. We show that for Gaussian states the answer is exactly $2k-1$ when the neighbors use Gaussian measurements, with any number of measurement settings. The limit follows from a simple bound. To every neighbor we assign a share, computed from the covariance matrix, and we prove that the shares of all neighbors add up to at most $k$, irrespective of the amount of squeezing, amplification or noise the network contains. A neighbor steers the node by Gaussian measurements exactly when its share exceeds one half, and a network built from a harmonic tight frame reaches the limit. The same number governs remote Wigner negativity. A heralded non-Gaussian operation at the node can make at most $2k-1$ neighbors Wigner negative, and in our network a single heralded projection makes all of them negative in the same run. With $n$ settings of arbitrary measurements, at most $nk-1$ neighbors can steer the node or violate a Bell inequality with it. More than $2k-1$ neighbors can therefore steer the node or violate a Bell inequality with it only if they use non-Gaussian measurements with at least three settings, whereas entanglement can reach any number of neighbors. These results determine exactly how many neighbors one multimode node can serve with steering and with remote Wigner negativity.

papers.title: Transition Path Sampling for Rare Events in Non-Markovian Open Quantum Systems
papers.abstract: Rare transitions govern the dynamics of many open quantum systems, but their probabilities and rates are difficult to calculate. Transition path sampling (TPS) of quantum systems has so far been limited to Markovian, perturbative descriptions. Here, we formulate TPS for non-Markovian quantum state diffusion, which is exact for Gaussian baths, extending it to non-Markovian and strongly coupled open quantum systems. For normal-to-superradiant tunneling in the unbalanced open Dicke model, we determine probabilities down to $10^{-8}$ and rates beyond the reach of brute force.

papers.title: The Price of Quantum Advantage in Computational Chemistry
papers.abstract: As the fault-tolerant era approaches, the question shifts from ``is it possible'' to ``is it worthwhile.'' To assess practical quantum advantage against reliable classical baselines, we examine 26 benchmark instances including FeMoco, iron-sulfur clusters, cytochrome P450, and ruthenium catalysts using two selected configuration interaction solvers, SHCI and TrimCI. Comparing classical workloads with fault-tolerant resource estimates, we calculate the break-even whole-QPU hourly price. Even at an optimistic price of US\$7{,}000 per whole-QPU hour, and with mid-range CPU clusters, classical computation remains cheaper for six of seven systems. FeMoco alone remains sensitive to the classical method and extrapolation strategy. Wavefunction analysis further reveals how orbital choice affects the determinant support required for target-state overlap in quantum phase estimation (QPE). Our results highlight the importance of reliable classical references and trial-state characterization, and quantify the economic conditions under which quantum computing can become competitive with classical alternatives.

papers.title: Neural Network Decoders For Qubit Loss
papers.abstract: Qubit loss is a significant source of error in many quantum hardware platforms, requiring circuits that periodically replace or reset qubits to maintain fault-tolerance. When the reset process includes loss-resolving measurements, this information can improve decoding and substantially reduce overhead compared to the case where this information is not available. Prior work has demonstrated loss-tolerant circuits for the surface code that show significantly improved thresholds and subthreshold scaling by incorporating loss information. However, the computational complexity of loss simulation and decoding, which falls outside of the usual stabilizer framework, has limited extending these studies to high-rate qLDPC codes, which are already challenging to decode in the absence of loss. In this work, we present a loss-aware convolutional neural-network (CNN) decoder framework that circumvents this challenge. Training is enabled by a novel sampler, \texttt{slim}, which achieves a throughput for circuits with Pauli noise and loss that is comparable to the state-of-the-art for pure Pauli noise. On the surface code with loss, the decoder matches the accuracy of computationally expensive most-likely error (MLE) decoders at much lower latency. For the $[[144,12,12]]$ bivariate bicycle (Gross) code, we study a walking syndrome extraction circuit with Pauli and loss errors. For physical error rates $p<1\%$, we observe a more than $10^3$-fold lower logical error rate for a pure loss model, relative to a pure Pauli error model at the same physical error rate, along with significantly enhanced sub-threshold error rate scaling. This demonstrates that loss-dominated error models can also significantly improve performance in a high-rate qLDPC code, and provides a simulation and decoder training platform that can be extended to other codes and algorithmic gadgets.

papers.title: The thermodynamic budget of objectivity
papers.abstract: An event becomes a fact when enough independent records of it exist such that no operation is possible that leaves all observers ignorant of it again. Records are physical, and creating, keeping, and destroying them have thermodynamic costs. We compute these costs exactly in a minimal broadcast model with a driven central qubit writing records into $N$ initially thermal registers, with work sources and baths at temperature $T$. The basic arguments for the operations are outlined here, with full treatment in the text. Creation of one event record at redundancy $R$ and information deficit $\delta$ requires work $W \ge R\, k_\mathrm{B}T \ln 2\, (1-\delta) H(\varepsilon)$, linear in redundancy at the Landauer coefficient. Recording in a basis misaligned by $\theta$ with the einselecting interaction fails at a critical angle, $\theta_c = 2\arcsin\sqrt{H_2^{-1}(\delta)}$, beyond which objectivity is unreachable at any work, and below $\theta_c$ the optimal work is a closed form in the pointer basis that minimizes the work of objectivity. Reducing objectivity is impossible at any work with access to fewer than $R - R_{\min} + 1$ records, while work protects nothing if given access. Inter-record redundancy is extractable free energy and erasing the accessed records yields a net gain of work beyond the first copy. The second law constrains the destruction of the correlation: erasing a fact from a sector an adversary controls dissipates at least the mutual information erased, but a consolidation dissipates nothing. Records in re-thermalizing media are nonequilibrium steady states, and the minimal power to maintain a record at $(R,\delta)$ is the known two-state driving bound evaluated at the record-quality boundary.

papers.title: Complementary mechanisms of critical quantum metrology
papers.abstract: Critical metrology conventionally exploits enhanced susceptibility to a system parameter near a phase transition. Here we identify a complementary mechanism for critically enhanced estimation of intrinsic system parameters via suppressed quantum noise rather than enhanced response. We demonstrate both mechanisms in coherently radiating spin states (CRSS)-correlated states of $N$ spin-$1/2$ particles defined as asymptotic eigenstates of the collective-spin lowering operator with complex eigenvalue $r e^{-i\varphi}$. At the critical value $r=1$, CRSS exhibit a second-order transition. We show that near criticality, estimation of $r$ benefits from enhanced susceptibility despite increased noise, whereas estimation of $\varphi$ benefits from suppressed quantum noise without enhanced response. Remarkably, both yield the same estimation error $\sim N^{-2/3}$, improving over the standard quantum limit $N^{-1/2}$. For $\varphi$, this establishes quantum-enhanced metrology of phases intrinsic to the critical system, rather than phases externally encoded by interferometry. We demonstrate these results for CRSS realizations in both dissipative (superradiant) and Hamiltonian (Ising) systems relevant to cavity QED and trapped ions, where fast preparation of CRSS is shown possible thanks to gap opening. Applications to metrology of coupling rates and phases or optical lengths are discussed.

papers.title: Bound Entanglement with Negative Partial Transpose Exists
papers.abstract: We show that the Werner state $\rho = (23 I - 3\,\mathrm{SWAP})/1448$ on $\mathbb{C}^8 \otimes \mathbb{C}^8$ has a negative partial transpose and is bound entangled: no LOCC protocol can distill entanglement from any number of copies of $\rho$, and even with separable operations the fidelity of a two-qubit output with a Bell state never exceeds $(1+\sqrt{2})/4 \approx 0.604$. It follows that distillable entanglement is neither additive nor convex.

papers.title: Schism: Reconfigurable Scale-Up Domains for Distributed Quantum Computing
papers.abstract: Switch-based quantum datacenters connect quantum processing units (QPUs) through photonic switches and shared Bell-state measurement (BSM) devices. Sharing BSMs saves hardware, but fixed connectivity constrains access to these resources. Local communication can overload one rack's BSMs while others remain idle; reaching those idle resources incurs additional optical loss and retries through switches and quantum frequency converters (QFCs). Programs remain locked into this locality-contention tradeoff as their communication patterns change. We propose Schism, an architecture that lets programs dynamically change which QPUs share each BSM pool. Schism places BSM pools at aggregation switches and QFCs on their core-facing uplinks. Top-of-rack switches establish reconfigurable native-wavelength circuits from QPUs to these pools, forming scale-up domains bounded by the optical loss budget. Reconfiguration reshapes resource sharing across racks without moving QPUs or migrating quantum states. Our key insight is that QPU grouping jointly determines photon-path loss and contention for BSM resources: locality alone cannot identify the best grouping, and a grouping pays off only if its savings outweigh the delay of reconfiguring to it. We develop an optimization framework that combines graph partitioning with resource-constrained completion-time estimates and dynamic programming to select how QPUs share BSM pools and when those groupings reconfigure, between or within circuit phases. Our evaluation using SeQUeNCe with trapped-ion parameters shows that Schism achieves communication speedups of 4.9-7.3x across 11 workloads on 32 QPUs compared to Fixed Clos connectivity and 3.6-8.3x compared to SwitchQNet. Schism also outperforms a hypothetical network-wide switch by 1.35-1.38x on the eight workloads whose phases fit in a pool, and trails it by 1.1-1.75x on the other three.

papers.title: A novel quantum lattice Boltzmann methodology for cosmological radiation transport
papers.abstract: Radiation transport is an essential process in many physical simulations, including cosmological codes which track stellar and diffuse radiation. Many present codes utilize ray tracing or moment methods, but these grow increasingly difficult and expensive for large simulations. Quantum lattice Boltzmann methods exponentially reduce complexity by propagating radiation over a lattice, allowing for better spatial resolution without needing to introduce adaptive ray tracing or other optimizations. However, existing formulations result in poor angular resolution for radiation point sources. In this work, we propose an angular redistribution methodology which significantly improves the resolution with minimal increase in complexity. We verify the correctness of the method on both classical processors and quantum simulators and outline how the quantum algorithm can be integrated into existing codes. This method is an important step towards fully-quantum radiation hydrodynamics simulation which could exponentially accelerate existing cosmological codes, enabling simulations at scales currently infeasible.

papers.title: Theory of Anomalous Diffusion and Superdiffusion in Integrable Spin Chains
papers.abstract: Integrable systems can exhibit diffusive or Kardar--Parisi--Zhang (KPZ) scaling in two-point correlations even when their current full counting statistics (FCS) differ from those usually associated with these universality classes. We explain this separation using a multispecies particle gas that preserves the scattering structure of integrable spin chains. For anisotropy $\Delta>1$, large particles are advected by a mobile bath. The resulting FCS has a Gaussian-mixture form and approaches the M-Wright distribution at late times, with finite-time rounding due to mobile species. At the isotropic point $\Delta=1$, all particles are mobile, and the charge transfer by large particles is discrete. A self-consistent Poisson distribution describes the FCS, with a nearly Gaussian bulk and model-dependent, non-Gaussian tails. By contrast, two-point correlations follow from the statistics of a large tracer particle. For $\Delta>1$, it undergoes Brownian motion, yielding Gaussian spreading. At $\Delta=1$, we provide evidence from fluctuating hydrodynamics for the emergence of the KPZ Pr\"ahofer--Spohn scaling function in dynamical correlations and trace it to the finite coupling of the largest particles to a continuum of slower ones, with long-ranged velocity fluctuations. Our framework shows how universal dynamical two-point correlations coexist with distinct model-dependent current statistics.

papers.title: Parton structure of mesonic states with tensor networks
papers.abstract: We present the first direct tensor network calculation of flavor-resolved parton distribution functions (PDFs) for a pion-like isospin triplet in the two-flavor Nambu-Jona-Lasinio model in (1+1) dimensions. Four-fermion interactions bind the mesons without confinement. Using staggered fermions and a charge-symmetrized Hamiltonian, we prepare the bound states and compute light-cone correlators by real-time evolution. The resulting quark and antiquark PDFs obey the expected isospin relations under $u \leftrightarrow d$ exchange between charged pions and exhibit equal u and d distributions in the neutral pion. A flavor-independent antisymmetrization of the field ordering removes the vacuum-subtracted anticommutator contribution and restores charge-conjugation relations in both the correlators and PDFs across the triplet within numerical accuracy. These results provide benchmarks for quantum simulations of the partonic structure of the meson.

papers.title: Energy plateau cascades from complex-time local quenches in thermal two-dimensional CFTs
papers.abstract: In this work, we study local operator quenches in thermal two-dimensional conformal field theories with complex-time evolution, which can be viewed as an effective description of conditional dynamics in a system interacting with an environment. In contrast to quenches of the vacuum, the thermal initial state allows several conformal families to participate in the evolution. We show that their competition can produce cascades of approximately homogeneous energy plateaux, with successive plateaux approaching the energies of different primary states. Using conformal Ward identities on the cylinder and torus, we determine the local energy density and illustrate this behavior in free-field theories, the Ising model and Wess--Zumino--Witten models. We develop a cold-limit spectral description in which the dominant primary channel determines the height of each plateau, while conformal dimensions and operator matrix elements govern the transitions between them. For a fixed compact unitary CFT, we show that only finitely many primary channels can contribute to the leading plateau sequence. Finally, we discuss the large-central-charge regime, relating light-operator plateaux to few-particle sectors in thermal AdS and examining the limitations of this picture for heavy quenches.

papers.title: Bosonic Magic Resources at Quantum Criticality
papers.abstract: Non-Gaussianity is a resource for bosonic quantum information processing, providing a necessary ingredient for universal quantum computation in continuous-variable systems. Here we quantify non-Gaussianity in the ground state of the one-dimensional extended Bose-Hubbard model using quantum relative entropy (QRE), a measure determined solely by one-body correlations. The scaling of the QRE with system size reveals quantum phase transitions involving hidden and conventional order. We connect QRE scaling in the weakly interacting superfluid phase to Luttinger-liquid correlations and identify distinct critical signatures in its extensive and subleading contributions. At the Mott-Haldane transition, subtracting the extensive background reveals a pronounced peak in the subleading contribution, providing a clear signature of the onset of hidden string order. At the Haldane-density-wave transition, the extensive contribution to the QRE instead exhibits scaling consistent with Ising criticality. These results establish non-Gaussianity as a probe of many-body criticality, linking bosonic quantum resources to strongly correlated matter.

papers.title: Modular fluctuation relations on local causal horizons
papers.abstract: Local causal horizons provide a setting for studying horizon thermodynamics in the neighborhood of any regular spacetime point. Here, we investigate this description beyond mean energy and entropy balances by studying fluctuations of boost-energy transfer induced by unitary perturbations of the horizon reference state. Using the modular structure of the horizon algebra and a thermal reference state, we construct an energy transfer probability measure and derive integral and detailed fluctuation relations with the mean entropy production being expressed in terms of the Araki relative entropy. The formulation accommodates type-III algebras without introducing a reduced density matrix and can be extended to global bifurcate Killing horizons admitting the required thermal reference state. For coherent scalar-field perturbations, we obtain a closed form for the characteristic function, identify the mean transfer with the excess boost-energy flux, and derive a thermodynamic uncertainty relation bounding the variance in terms of the mean transfer. We then explore the geometric implications by postulating a stochastic horizon entropy--area correspondence that associates an area change with each counted energy transfer. Under this additional hypothesis, we obtain fluctuation relations for area changes and an area change uncertainty bound for coherent perturbations.

papers.title: Superconductivity from the Berry connection from many-electron wave functions: $U(1)$ gauge fluctuation, gauge invariance, and superconductivity
papers.abstract: The electromagnetic $U(1)$ gauge invariance and superconductivity are examined by employing the Berry connection from many-electron wave functions and the fluctuations of it that give rise to the probabilistic random transitions among quantum states. The gauge invariance in the classical electrodynamics is regarded as the requirement that extracts unaffected parts by the gauge fluctuation. In quantum mechanics, dissipation-free states from the gauge fluctuation exist, and we identify them as superconducting states. We explain the reversible superconducting-normal phase transition in a magnetic field including the force balance. The present superconductivity theory lifts two fundamental disagreements between theory and experiment existing in the current standard theory with keeping the major results by the BCS theory. Thus, it may be considered as a superconductivity theory encompassing the current standard one.

papers.title: Late-time OTOCs in Toda conformal field theory
papers.abstract: We study late-time out-of-time-order correlators (OTOCs) of semi-degenerate primary fields in two-dimensional $A_{N-1}$ Toda conformal field theory. In Liouville theory ($N=2$), we find that the OTOC decays as $t^{-3/2}$ when the continuum edge dominates, correcting a previously reported constant limit. For $N=3$, a transverse contour pinch reduces the spectral integral to one dimension. Assuming that the reduced expansion is complete, in the continuous phase the regulated edge behaves as a discrete state, and the OTOC approaches a pure braiding phase. As we check numerically, the edge block is a free-field correlator in a charge-neutral Weyl frame; this explains the pure phase and is consistent with crossing symmetry. For both $N=2$ and $N=3$, a dominant discrete residue gives a constant late-time limit. For $N\geq4$, the same one-dimensional reduction violates a crossing bound on the lowest intermediate weight of a positive diagonal expansion. Hence the $N=2,3$ phase diagram does not extend to higher rank without additional contributions below the reduced continuum edge or outside a positive diagonal expansion.

papers.title: TyxonQ: A Workflow Layer for Quantum Computing in Chemistry
papers.abstract: Quantum computational chemistry is often framed around a hybrid quantum solver. In practical applications, however, bottlenecks to adoption also lie in the surrounding multiscale workflow. A molecular problem may combine classical molecular mechanics and dynamics, conventional electronic-structure calculations, and a quantum solver for selected orbitals or embedded fragments. This division of work is particularly relevant when a chemically important electronic subspace is strongly correlated. The size of the electronic Hilbert space and the qubit, noise, and circuit-depth constraints of noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices make active-space and embedding choices central to a feasible quantum calculation. The resulting energies and gradients must remain consistent with the surrounding classical simulation. We present TyxonQ, a workflow layer that connects these levels of treatment rather than addressing only the hybrid quantum algorithm. Four integration interfaces link PySCF-compatible energy/force scanners and embedding, solver adapters, simulator and hardware backends, and classical consumers. The implementation combines QM/MM and fragment embedding with conventional CCSD/FCI fragment solvers, variational and sampling-based quantum methods, and adapters for ASE, i-PI, OpenMM, LAMMPS (through i-PI), and MDI. We describe the contracts and audit coverage, and evaluate correctness, switching cost, reproducibility, and artifact portability on small chemistry workflows, distinguishing executed paths from source-level support. The purpose of TyxonQ is to support incremental integration of quantum calculations into existing computational chemistry workflows, including those used in industry, while retaining appropriate classical treatments elsewhere.

papers.title: Coherent quantum-circuit simulation of Mueller dipole branching at small $x$: multiplicity fluctuations and DIS phenomenology
papers.abstract: Mueller dipole branching at small $x$ is a stochastic process in which splitting rates depend on transverse geometry. We construct a coherent quantum circuit for a regulated finite-state version of this process. Poisson-clock uniformization controls the number of updates, while orthogonal event-history registers retain the splitting paths, including those leading to the same final configuration. The circuit prepares transition amplitudes from local splitting rates rather than loading a precomputed evolved distribution. Its statevector multiplicity probabilities reproduce the truncated-clock Markov result to numerical precision and agree with the full continuous-time Markov-chain benchmark within approximately $7\times10^{-4}$. To examine fluctuations beyond the small circuit, we independently simulate the Mueller cascade with continuous transverse coordinates. At the largest rapidity studied, its normalized fourth factorial moment is $1.81$, compared with $2.84$ for an equal-mean Yule process. We also determine multiplicity entropies and correlations between dipole-size sectors. Applying a fixed negative-binomial dipole-to-charged-particle response reproduces the rising trend of the H1 charged-particle multiplicity entropy toward smaller $x$, but does not fully describe the measured multiplicity distributions. These results demonstrate an explicit coherent encoding of finite-state dipole branching and clarify its relation to continuous-cascade fluctuations and DIS phenomenology.

papers.title: The transverse spin-gradient approximation in noncollinear spin density functional theory
papers.abstract:
We prove a quantitative error bound for a fixed-axis variant of the transverse spin-gradient approximation (TSGA) in noncollinear spin density functional theory. Inspired by Eich and Gross, we use a spin-spiral wave (SSW) as the local reference for the grand-canonical Levy-Lieb energy with the Hartree term subtracted. We construct the thermodynamic limit of the electron gas with constant total density and a prescribed SSW magnetization. Its energy per unit volume $e_{m SSW}$ is evaluated at the local wavevector $
abla\varphi$, where $\varphi$ is the spiral phase. When $\varphi$ is the azimuthal angle of the magnetization $\mathbf{m}=(m_1,m_2,m_3)$, the approximation reads \[ E(ho,\mathbf{m})\approx\int_{\mathbb{R}^3}e_{m SSW} ig(ho(\mathbf{x}),\mathbf{m}(\mathbf{x}),
abla\varphi(\mathbf{x}) ig)\,d \mathbf{x}. \] Here $
abla\varphi$ measures the local rotation of $\mathbf{m}$ about the third axis. Wherever $m_1^2+m_2^2>0$, it equals $(m_1
abla m_2-m_2
abla m_1)/(m_1^2+m_2^2)$. The approximation thus depends only on the total density $ho$, the magnetization and its first derivatives. When the spin-polarized density in the rotating frame and the local wavevector vary on the length scale $N^{1/3}$, with $N$ the mean number of particles, we obtain an error $O(N^{5/6})$ for an energy of order $N$. Setting the phase to zero gives the noncollinear local spin density approximation (LSDA) for arbitrary magnetization directions.

papers.title: Intrinsically nonlinear nanomechanical resonator toward the single-phonon Kerr regime
papers.abstract: Manipulating a physical system at the single-quantum level typically requires an anharmonic energy spectrum. Nanomechanical resonators, however, are commonly admitted to be linear objects in the single-phonon regime, thus motivating most efforts to employ external sources of nonlinearity at the cost of added relaxation and decoherence channels. Here, we take a radically different approach by directly exploiting strong intrinsic mechanical nonlinearities. We quantify this nonlinearity using a novel method based on the coupling between bending modes. Using this technique, we establish an upper bound of 34.0 +/- 9.7 phonons for the onset of intrinsically mechanical bistability. In addition, we highlight a new tuning mechanism based on a mechanical polarization angle of an upward-buckled nanotube resonator allowing us to reach an optimal working point. Extrapolating this level of intrinsic nonlinearity to realistically shorter resonators shows that the single-phonon Kerr regime is within reach, allowing for the realization of purely mechanical Schr\"odinger-cat states and highly coherent mechanical qubits.

papers.title: Conditional multiparameter thermometry with neutrino oscillations: MSW energy diversity and a plasma-noise benchmark
papers.abstract: We address temperature-parameter inference in a restricted two-flavor neutrino dephasing model with fixed mean electron densities. When two zone temperatures enter the propagated state via a single accumulated dephasing exponent, the single-energy quantum Fisher information matrix has rank at most 1. Independent, energy-resolved samples restore regular local identifiability when their thermal-sensitivity vectors are noncollinear. Matter-dependent mixing provides distinct weights in an illustrative two-zone model. A separate two-probe benchmark shows how complementary Bell sectors can distinguish temperature from spatial noise correlations. An electron-only Debye-cell estimate gives a conditional longitudinal quantum signal-to-noise ratio of approximately $3.1\times10^{-13}$ at 10 MeV for a uniform central-density medium over one solar radius. This estimate is not a microscopic upper bound or a detector sensitivity forecast. Complete phase averaging removes temperature information carried solely by longitudinal coherence damping; to retain solar sensitivity, a separate calculation of population, refractive, or production effects is required. The results distinguish conditional state identifiability from operational temperature inference.

papers.title: Data-enhanced self-learning projective quantum Monte Carlo with Rydberg-atom measurements
papers.abstract: We introduce a data-enhanced self-learning projective quantum Monte Carlo (PQMC) method that incorporates projective measurements from programmable quantum simulators into the guiding wavefunction of a ground-state projection. We demonstrate the approach for a two-dimensional Rydberg-atom array using restricted Boltzmann machine (RBM) and recurrent neural network (RNN) guiding wavefunctions. Experimental pretraining reduces finite-population effects and accelerates self-learning convergence, allowing unbiased estimation of ground-state properties to be obtained with fewer walkers and fewer self-learning iterations. The improvement is particularly pronounced for the RBM, while the more accurate RNN guiding wavefunction exhibits a smaller, though still observable, benefit from pretraining. Simulations across different system sizes suggest that the relative advantage of experimental pretraining may increase with system size. Improvements are also observed for the checkerboard order parameter, despite deviations of the experimental measurements from the equilibrium numerical results. Finally, finite-size scaling with self-learning PQMC without experimental pretraining yields the critical point and critical exponents of the disordered-to-checkerboard transition in agreement with previous numerical studies. Our results show that limited and imperfect experimental measurements can provide an effective initialization for self-learning PQMC, while imaginary-time projection combined with subsequent unsupervised learning progressively refines the guiding wavefunction toward the ground state.

papers.title: The asymptotic spectrum of tensors is connected
papers.abstract: We prove path-connectedness of the asymptotic spectrum of complex tensors of every fixed order $k \geq 3$: every spectral point is connected by a path to every "one leg versus the rest" flattening rank. In particular, the asymptotic spectrum evaluated at any fixed tensor is a closed interval, answering a question of Strassen. This was previously known only on specific families of tensors (Strassen, FOCS 1986, Crelle 1987-1991; Wigderson and Zuiddam, Bull. AMS 2026) or for specific families of spectral points (Christandl, Vrana and Zuiddam, STOC 2018; Sakabe, Do\u{g}an and Walter, FOCS 2026; Alman, Li and Pratt, FOCS 2026). To obtain our path-connectedness theorem we develop a general method for "interpolating" between spectral points, which applies to Strassen semirings that are appropriately decomposable (in the sense of an information-theoretic "method of types" on the semiring) and whose spectral points satisfy a cover property (inspired by slice rank). This covers tensors and asymptotic rank (with "types" given by decomposition into symmetric group irreps), as well as other objects and asymptotic problems, like graphs and Shannon capacity, where it matches the interpolation of Vrana (2019). Using our interpolation methods we furthermore obtain new results and simpler proofs of previous results regarding the asymptotic spectrum of rectangular matrix multiplication, polynomial multiplication and non-crossing (laminar) quantum functionals.

papers.title: Rényi multi-entropy from Riemann surfaces
papers.abstract: We compute vacuum tripartite R\'enyi multi-entropy in a two-dimensional compact-boson conformal field theory (CFT). For every integer R\'enyi index $n\geq2$, we evaluate the partition function on the replica Riemann surface for disjoint intervals, obtaining the twist four-point function in terms of a ratio of theta functions. An independent calculation of the partition function on a Fermat curve yields the adjacent three-point coefficient. In the fusion limit, the Riemann surface for disjoint intervals degenerates into two Fermat curves, and the residue of the four-point function reproduces the squared three-point coefficient, as required by the operator product expansion. The genuine multi-entropy therefore approaches twice its strictly adjacent value. The CFT predictions agree with lattice calculations for the critical XXZ and Ising spin chains and a harmonic chain. We also exhibit a unitary CFT in which the canonical replica construction yields complex R\'enyi multi-entropy.

papers.title: $\mathsf{AC}^0 \not\subseteq \mathsf{BQAC}^0/\mathsf{qpoly}$ via Sublinear-Degree Pauli Approximation
papers.abstract: We prove $\mathsf{AC}^0 \not\subseteq \mathsf{BQAC}^0/\mathsf{qpoly}$ in the single-copy, single-output model via an explicit $\mathsf{P}$-uniform family of linear-size monotone depth-2 CNFs. Every $\mathsf{QAC}^0$ circuit with arbitrary quantum advice achieves only an inverse-polynomial worst-case advantage over random guessing on this family. To prove this, we approximate the acceptance operator of any such circuit in operator norm by an advice-independent Hermitian operator of sublinear Pauli degree on a designated register alone, with degree exponent independent of width. Product-projection localization and Pauli twirling produce an auxiliary-register spectral cutoff that folds into contractions during backward peeling. The same approximation yields two stretched-exponential bounds against $\mathsf{QAC}^0$ circuits on $m$-qubit states. First, given polynomially many copies and input-independent quantum advice, single-output circuits distinguish exact or exponentially approximate state $2$-designs from Haar-random states with advantage at most $e^{-m^\alpha}$. Second, any state prepared from fewer than $k$ arbitrary input qubits and remaining $|0\rangle$ inputs has spectral weight at most $2e^{-m^\alpha}$ in a constant-energy-density band of an Anshu--Breuckmann--Nirkhe NLTS Hamiltonian encoding $k$ logical qubits. Both bounds hold for every fixed $\alpha\in(0,1)$.

papers.title: Monotonic probes of asymmetry and robustness of the quantum Mpemba effect
papers.abstract: Entanglement asymmetry has emerged as a powerful probe of symmetry restoration and the quantum Mpemba effect. However, its conventional R\'enyi generalizations, defined as differences of R\'enyi entropies, are not monotones in the resource-theoretic sense. Here, we investigate an alternative family of asymmetry quantifiers based on sandwiched R\'enyi divergences, which satisfy monotonicity under symmetry-preserving quantum channels. Developing a two-parameter replica approach, we show how these quantities can be computed from charged moments and establish a remarkable correspondence with conventional R\'enyi asymmetries under the inversion of the R\'enyi index, $\alpha\leftrightarrow 1/\alpha$. This relation, exact for pure states, holds at leading order in the relevant scaling limits for homogeneous quantum quenches, including interacting integrable systems, and for Haar-random states. Applying these results to quenches from tilted ferromagnetic states, we demonstrate that the quantum Mpemba effect is remarkably robust, occurring throughout the entire family of sandwiched R\'enyi asymmetry monotones. We identify dynamical regimes in quenches from spatially inhomogeneous initial states where conventional R\'enyi asymmetries and genuine monotones exhibit qualitatively different behaviours. We also investigate a solvable toy model illustrating the possible dependence of Mpemba crossings on the R\'enyi index. Our findings establish a connection between conventional R\'enyi asymmetries and quantum resource theory, explaining their effectiveness in broad classes of nonequilibrium protocols while highlighting the additional information provided by genuine asymmetry monotones.

papers.title: Schrödinger's Legacy: The Wave Function and Quantum Reality
papers.abstract: The article discusses how Schr\"odinger arrived at the formulation of wave mechanics and his legacy on the philosophy of quantum mechanics, focusing in particular on the metaphysics of the wave function. Schr\"odinger's interpretation of the wave function as electron charge density is generally dismissed or presented only as a curious historical example in the literature. On a closer look, however, while this interpretation was eventually abandoned in favor of Born's statistical interpretation, Schr\"odinger's idea survived in modern realist approaches to the wave function, such as the mass-density approach and the multi-field interpretation. It also proved to be of great utility in modern techniques and approximations in quantum chemistry to compute the shape of atoms and molecules. Overall, Schr\"odinger's interpretation of the wave function and his realist understanding of quantum mechanics paved the way to modern attempts to define a clear ontology of the microscopic world, a tradition that survived the Copenhagen interpretation of Bohr and Heisenberg and that is still present today.

papers.title: Vacuum correlation measures as CFT partition functions
papers.abstract: We show that in any $d$-dimensional CFT, the vacuum sandwiched R\'enyi mutual information (SRMI) of integer order $n$ between two disjoint balls maps to a CFT partition function on a manifold of topology $\#^{n-1}(S^1 \times S^{d-1})$, with moduli fixed by the ball configuration and single-ball modular flow. At $n=2$, it is given by the thermal partition function on $S^{d-1}$, upper-bounding the von Neumann mutual information. For $n>2$, SRMI diverges at finite separation due to a hot-spot limit of the partition function. Explicit CFT evaluations agree well with density matrix computations.
